text:
All the data from Redis 7.2 is now on the Valkey 9.1 server, and Valkey is running as a standalone primary that accepts writes.

**How I copied it:** I made Valkey (port 6380) a temporary replica of Redis (port 6379) with `REPLICAOF 127.0.0.1 6379`. That copies the full dataset, including key types, remaining time to live and stream consumer groups. Once the copy finished, I ran `REPLICAOF NO ONE` to turn Valkey back into an independent primary.

**Checks:**
- I compared every key in every database on both servers with a script, once while Valkey was still a replica and again after it became independent. Both runs found 0 differences out of 3,270 keys:
  - db0 has 2,920 keys and db2 has 350.
  - By type: 2,345 strings, 450 hashes, 155 sorted sets, 150 sets, 150 lists and 20 streams.
  - It checked that each key exists on both, has the same type and value, and has a time to live within 5 seconds of the original.
  - For streams it also checked consumer groups, pending entries, consumers and stream metadata.
- A test write to Valkey worked, and I deleted the test key afterwards.
- `/etc/valkey/valkey.conf` has no `replicaof` line, so Valkey will stay a primary after a restart.
- I saved Valkey's data to disk (`BGSAVE`).

**Redis:** It is still running as a primary with no replicas attached, and I didn't write anything to it. The copy only read from it, though it did make Redis take a background snapshot.

**Before the switch:** Valkey is now separate from Redis, so anything written to Redis from here on won't reach Valkey. Stop writes to Redis before you point applications at Valkey, or recent changes will be missing. The comparison script is at `/tmp/cmp.py` if you want to run it again just before switching.
